svg.title: P11: Tool-workflow boundary
svg.desc: Analytical UML class view of the proposed pattern contract; not an observed implementation or execution trace.
svg.text: Primitive / UML CLASS VIEW / ANALYTICAL MODEL

text.tspan: Distinguish an operation from an orchestration.

svg.text: dashed arrow: call dependency · brown: return/failure · analytical, not an observed trace

text.tspan: The harness exposes both primitive effects and multi-step procedures.
The agent chooses a tool or workflow entry point.
Separate effect/result contracts and workflow ownership of sequencing.
Workflow orchestration is not mistaken for a single external side effect.
Tool and workflow descriptors have distinct schemas and execution paths.
Retry, budget, and result accounting bind to the correct unit.
A workflow cannot hide duplicate irreversible tool effects.
Nested failures and retries produce explicit ownership and cost records.
1 Agent → ToolBoundary choose(operation)
2 ToolBoundary → Tool invoke(effect)
3 Tool ↩ ToolBoundary return(effect)
4 Agent → WorkflowEngine choose(orchestration)
5 WorkflowEngine → Tool invoke(step)
6 WorkflowEngine → CostMeter account(workflow)
7 ToolBoundary → CostMeter account(effect)
8 ToolBoundary → Agent return(result)
9 WorkflowEngine → Agent return(result)
Workflow DSL, composite tool, procedure service, and sub-agent workflow.
Test retry inside workflow, duplicate steps, and result aggregation.
A single function that happens to call another function is not enough.
